t.1.182.1: Having gone to that potter's workshop and reached Pṛthā, the two illustrious sons of Pṛthā, foremost among men, supremely delighted, then announced Yājñasenī to her as alms.
t.1.182.3: Fearing unrighteousness and deeply ashamed, Kuntī took by the hand Yājñasenī, who was supremely glad, approached Yudhiṣṭhira, and spoke these words.
t.1.182.2: She, inside the hut, without looking at her sons, said, "Enjoy it, all of you together." But afterward, when Kuntī saw the maiden, she said, "What I have said is terrible."
t.1.182.4: For this maiden, daughter of King Drupada, was handed over to me by your two younger brothers, and I too, son, out of carelessness, said as was my habit, “Enjoy it together,” O king.
t.1.182.6: But after reflecting for only a moment, King Yudhiṣṭhira of supreme vigor, the foremost hero of the Kurus, comforted his mother Kuntī and spoke these words to Dhanaṃjaya.
t.1.182.5: Tell me, O bull among the Kurus, how what I have said today may not become a falsehood, and how no unrighteousness, such as has never happened before, may befall the daughter of the king of the Pāñcālas.
t.1.182.7: O Pāṇḍava, it was you who won Yājñasenī, and with you the princess will be content. Let the fire be kindled and the oblations be offered into it; take her hand according to the rite.
t.1.182.8: O lord of men, do not make me a partaker of unrighteousness, for this is not the dharma that others desire. You should be married first, and after you this Bhīma, mighty-armed and of inconceivable deeds.
t.1.182.10: This being so, consider well what ought to be done here that is righteous and brings glory, and do that; and tell us what would be pleasing to the king of the Pāñcālas, for we all stand under your command.
t.1.182.9: Then I, and after me Nakula, and last Sahadeva, the son of Mādrī. Vṛkodara, I and the twins, O king, and this maiden too, all of us are yours.
t.1.182.11: All of them, seeing the glorious Kṛṣṇā standing there, looked at one another as they sat and held her in their hearts.
t.1.182.12: For when all of them, of boundless might, beheld Draupadī, Manobhava, the mind-born god of love, arose within them, overpowering the whole host of their senses.
t.1.182.13: For the lovely form of Pāñcālī, fashioned by the Creator himself, surpassed that of all other women and captivated the hearts of all beings.
t.1.182.15: For the king, fearing discord among them, said to those brothers: "The lovely Draupadī shall be the wife of all of us."
t.1.182.14: O bull among men, Kuntī's son Yudhiṣṭhira, who understood their outward signs and their inner feelings, called to mind the whole of Dvaipāyana's words.
